LESSON: WRITING 5.4.1 HANDWRITING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.4: Writing 5.4.1 Handwriting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.4.1 Handwriting, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to write clearly and neatly? 2. How can we tell letters are correctly written?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.4.1 Handwriting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learner’s self- discipline is enhanced as they work collaboratively to practise shaping letters and writing words from left to

right.

Values:
Unity is enhanced as the learner collaborates with others during language game activities.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Self -esteem is nurtured as learners write legibly for effective communication.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Kiswahili Language Activities as learners form letters in terms of shape and size and write words from left to right to communicate effectively.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners,

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.

Suggested Vocabulary:

sun, shine, rain, clouds, blow, wind, grow, cut, grass, cloudy, windy, sunny, rainy
